title: Measurement comparability
responsibility: Determines whether a measurement and baseline describe the same quantity and sampling method before their numeric values are compared.

inputs.name: comparisonDifferences.metric
inputs.description: Metric name looked up in metricUnits: latency-cold-ms, latency-warm-ms and latency-floor-ms expect ms, throughput-ops expects ops/s and memory-bytes expects bytes. Any other name only requires the two units to be equal, and an inherited Object.prototype name such as constructor always reports a unit difference because the lookup returns a non-string value.

inputs.name: comparisonDifferences.measured
inputs.description: The current measurement's unitOfMeasure, method and comparison: an empty or missing unitOfMeasure or method, or a missing or invalid comparison, is listed in differences and makes the verdict incomplete. A valid comparison has exactly the fields request (a sha256 hex digest of 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters), boundary (public-invocation or fixture), protocol (a string with at least one character after trimming) and sampling, and sampling has exactly warmup (a non-negative integer), rounds and iterations (integers of at least 1).

examples.method: warm-up calls, then rounds of timed whole invocations
warm-up calls, then rounds of timed whole invocations

inputs.name: comparisonDifferences.baseline
inputs.description: The baseline's unitOfMeasure, method and comparison, checked by the same rules as the measurement and reported under the name baseline when missing or invalid. For a comparable verdict each must equal the measurement's.

examples.method: warm-up calls, then rounds of timed whole invocations
warm-up calls, then rounds of timed whole invocations

outputs.name: comparisonDifferences
outputs.description: Status is comparable, with an empty differences list, when both sides state a unit of measure, a method and a valid comparison and no difference is found. Status is incomplete when either side lacks or invalidly states one of those, and differences then lists each such item, measurement first, in the order comparison, unit of measure, method; otherwise status is incompatible and differences lists each mismatch in the order unit of measure, request, boundary, protocol, sampling, method.

differences: the measurement states no comparison context
request 9c4e1a7f3b0d differs from the baseline request d61b8f2a0c7e
sampling is 10 rounds of 100 calls after 3 warm-up calls, the baseline used 10 rounds of 50 calls after 3 warm-up calls
